question: A gut bacterium calmed stressed mice through the vagus nerve. What did it do in healthy men?
answer: No measurable effect. In 2011, Lactobacillus rhamnosus JB-1 reduced anxious behaviour and stress hormones in mice, and cutting the vagus nerve abolished the effect. In 2017 the same strain, given to 29 healthy men for eight weeks against a placebo, changed neither their stress response nor their scores on mood and thinking tests.
move: A finding travels only as far as the subjects it was tested on.
ask: Which finding am I applying to myself when it was only tested on someone unlike me?
trap: Expecting a clean result in mice to carry over to people.
source: Kelly et al., Brain, Behavior, and Immunity, 2017
reference: Kelly, Allen, Temko et al., Lost in translation? The potential psychobiotic Lactobacillus rhamnosus (JB-1) fails to modulate stress or cognitive performance in healthy male subjects, Brain, Behavior, and Immunity, 2017
